differential: Myasthenia gravis
Double vision (diplopia) in a young adult is a classic presenting symptom of this autoimmune neuromuscular disorder affecting ocular muscles.
Multiple sclerosis
Demyelinating lesions affecting cranial nerves or brainstem pathways can cause binocular diplopia in this age group.
Cranial nerve VI palsy
Isolated abducens nerve palsy from microvascular, inflammatory, or idiopathic causes presents with horizontal diplopia.
Thyroid eye disease (Graves' ophthalmopathy)
Inflammatory infiltration of extraocular muscles can cause restrictive diplopia, even without overt hyperthyroidism.
Brainstem stroke or ischemia
Vascular events affecting cranial nerve nuclei or internuclear pathways can produce acute diplopia in adults.
eliminated: None
Insufficient information at this stage to definitively rule out any diagnoses.

differential: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
Classic triad of ophthalmoplegia (diplopia), ataxia (broad-based gait), and confusion in chronic alcohol abuse with memory impairment and confabulation.
Cerebellar degeneration (alcohol-related)
Chronic alcohol abuse causing nystagmus and ataxia, though does not fully explain cognitive symptoms and confabulation.
Hepatic encephalopathy
Confusion, personality changes, and ataxia can occur in chronic alcoholics with liver disease, though ophthalmoplegia is less typical.
Chronic subdural hematoma
Gait disturbance, confusion, and personality changes in alcoholic patient prone to falls, though bilateral ophthalmoplegia would be unusual.
Marchiafava-Bignami disease
Rare demyelinating disorder associated with chronic alcoholism causing cognitive decline and gait abnormalities.
eliminated: Acute stroke
Vital signs stable and symptoms have evolved over a week rather than acutely.
Multiple sclerosis
Age and clinical presentation with chronic alcoholism makes Wernicke-Korsakoff far more likely.

differential: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
Decreased erythrocyte transketolase activity and mammillary body atrophy are pathognomonic for thiamine deficiency with chronic alcoholism causing this combined encephalopathy-amnestic syndrome.
Wernicke encephalopathy
The classic triad of ophthalmoplegia (diplopia, nystagmus), ataxia (broad-based gait), and confusion with alcohol abuse and decreased transketolase activity are diagnostic.
Korsakoff syndrome
Mammillary body atrophy, confabulation, severe memory impairment, and personality changes (indifference, agitation) in chronic alcoholism represent the chronic amnestic phase of thiamine deficiency.
Alcoholic cerebellar degeneration
Chronic alcohol abuse with ataxia and broad-based gait could suggest cerebellar degeneration, though this doesn't fully explain the ocular findings and cognitive impairment.
Hepatic encephalopathy
Chronic alcoholism can cause liver disease leading to encephalopathy with confusion and personality changes, though the specific laboratory and imaging findings point elsewhere.
eliminated: Acute stroke
MRI shows chronic atrophy rather than acute vascular lesions, and the symptom progression over weeks is inconsistent with acute cerebrovascular event.
Multiple sclerosis
Patient's age and sex could fit, but decreased transketolase activity and mammillary body atrophy are specific for thiamine deficiency, not demyelinating disease.
Alcohol intoxication
While patient has alcohol abuse history, the specific laboratory findings and structural brain changes indicate a chronic thiamine deficiency state rather than acute intoxication.

differential: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome

Chronic alcoholism with classic triad (ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, confusion), decreased transketolase activity, mammillary body atrophy, and dramatic response to thiamine confirm thiamine deficiency encephalopathy.
Alcohol-related dementia
Chronic alcohol abuse with memory impairment, personality changes, and cognitive decline, though this would not explain the acute ophthalmoplegia or rapid thiamine response.
Marchiafava-Bignami disease
Rare alcohol-related corpus callosum demyelination can present with confusion and gait disturbance, but mammillary body atrophy and thiamine response point away from this.
Hepatic encephalopathy
Chronic alcoholism can cause liver failure with confusion and personality changes, but would not explain nystagmus, ophthalmoplegia, or mammillary body atrophy.
Alcoholic cerebellar degeneration
Chronic alcohol use causing ataxia and gait disturbance, but would not explain ophthalmoplegia, mammillary body atrophy, or rapid thiamine response.
eliminated: Stroke (posterior circulation)
Acute thiamine response and bilateral mammillary body atrophy inconsistent with vascular etiology.
Multiple sclerosis
Mammillary body atrophy, decreased transketolase activity, and dramatic thiamine response rule out demyelinating disease.
Brain tumor
MRI showing only mammillary body atrophy without mass lesion and rapid thiamine response exclude neoplasm.

differential: Myasthenia gravis
Diplopia is a classic presenting symptom in adults, often with fluctuating weakness of extraocular muscles.
Sixth nerve palsy
Unilateral or bilateral abducens nerve dysfunction commonly presents with binocular horizontal diplopia.
Multiple sclerosis
Young adults can present with diplopia from internuclear ophthalmoplegia or cranial nerve involvement due to demyelinating lesions.
Thyroid eye disease
Orbital inflammation and extraocular muscle enlargement can cause restrictive diplopia, even in subclinical thyroid dysfunction.
Intracranial mass lesion
A tumor or other space-occupying lesion affecting cranial nerves III, IV, or VI could present with isolated diplopia.
Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
Chronic alcoholism with confusion, memory impairment, confabulation, and gait disturbance are classic features, though classic triad is incomplete.
Alcoholic cerebellar degeneration
Chronic alcohol abuse with broad-based gait and cognitive changes, though lack of ataxia on exam is atypical.
Hepatic encephalopathy
Confusion, personality changes, and gait disturbance in chronic alcoholic could indicate liver failure with encephalopathy.
Marchiafava-Bignami disease
Rare alcohol-related corpus callosum demyelination presenting with confusion, personality changes, and gait abnormalities.
Alcohol-related dementia
Progressive cognitive decline, personality changes, confabulation, and memory impairment in setting of chronic heavy alcohol use.
eliminated: Wernicke encephalopathy (acute)
Absence of the classic triad (nystagmus, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxia documented on exam) makes isolated acute Wernicke less likely than the chronic Korsakoff component.

differential: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome

Decreased erythrocyte transketolase activity and mammillary body atrophy in a chronic alcohol abuser with confabulation, memory impairment, and confusion are pathognomonic for thiamine deficiency-related encephalopathy.
Korsakoff syndrome (chronic phase)
Prominent confabulation, memory impairment, and mammillary body atrophy suggest the chronic amnestic phase of thiamine deficiency, though acute Wernicke features are less evident.
Alcoholic dementia

Chronic alcohol abuse with personality changes (indifference, agitation) and cognitive impairment could represent direct alcohol-related brain damage, though laboratory findings favor thiamine deficiency.
Hepatic encephalopathy

Confusion and personality changes in a chronic alcohol abuser could indicate liver dysfunction, though the specific laboratory findings and imaging are more consistent with Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
Marchiafava-Bignami disease
Rare alcohol-related demyelination disorder can present with confusion and cognitive impairment in chronic alcoholics, though mammillary body atrophy is not typical.
eliminated: Wernicke encephalopathy (acute, isolated)
Classic triad of ophthalmoplegia, nystagmus, and ataxia are explicitly absent on examination.
Multiple sclerosis
Decreased transketolase activity and mammillary body atrophy are not consistent with demyelinating disease.
Stroke
Acute onset and vascular distribution would not explain progressive symptoms, decreased transketolase activity, or bilateral mammillary body atrophy.

differential: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
